column1: The threat posed by climate change in the Arctic and the problems faced by Canada’s Inuit people
column2: 气候变化对北极地区构成的威胁，以及加拿大因纽特人面临的问题

column1: Unusual incidents are being reported across the Arctic.
column2: 在北极地区，人们报告了各种异常事件

column1: Inuit families going off on snowmobiles to prepare their summer hunting camps have found themselves cut off from home by a sea of mud, following early thaws.
column2: 有些因纽特家庭骑雪地摩托出去准备夏季狩猎营地，却发现冰雪提早消融，遍地泥泞，回家的路被阻断了。
column7: a sea of mud|一大片泥泞

column1: There are reports of igloos losing their insulating properties as the snow drips and refreezes, of lakes draining into the sea as permafrost melts, and sea ice breaking up earlier than usual, carrying seals beyond the reach of hunters.
column2: 有消息说，积雪融化滴落后又结冰，冰屋因此失去了隔热性能，永久冻土融化，湖水由此流入海里，海冰也比往年更早破裂，载着海豹漂到了猎人够不到的地方。
column16: beyond the reach of|在……够不到的地方

column1: Climate change may still be a rather abstract idea to most of us, but in the Arctic it is already having dramatic effects — if summertime ice continues to shrink at its present rate, the Arctic Ocean could soon become virtually ice-free in summer.
column2: 对我们大多数人来说，气候变化可能仍是个相当抽象的概念，但它已给北极带来显著影响。如果夏季海冰继续以目前的速度消退，北冰洋或许很快就会在夏天几乎没有海冰。
column7: at its present rate|按目前的速度

column1: The knock-on effects are likely to include more warming, cloudier skies, increased precipitation and higher sea levels.
column2: 这些连锁反应可能包括气温进一步升高、天空变得更阴沉、降水量增加以及海平面上升等问题。

column1: Scientists are increasingly keen to find out what’s going on because they consider the Arctic the ‘canary in the mine’ for global warming — a warning of what’s in store for the rest of the world.
column2: 科学家们越来越想弄清楚北极正在发生什么，因为他们把北极看作全球变暖的“矿井里的金丝雀”，它预示着世界其他地方将会面临什么。
column6: canary in the mine|早期预警信号
column9: in store for|即将发生在……身上
column10: rest of the world|世界其他地方

column1: For the Inuit the problem is urgent.
column2: 对于因纽特人来说，这个问题非常紧迫。

column1: They live in precarious balance with one of the toughest environments on earth.
column2: 他们生活在与地球上最恶劣环境之一之间的微妙平衡之中。

column1: Climate change, whatever its causes, is a direct threat to their way of life.
column2: 无论气候变化的原因是什么，它都直接威胁着他们的生活方式。

column1: Nobody knows the Arctic as well as the locals, which is why they are not content simply to stand back and let outside experts tell them what’s happening.
column2: 没有人比当地居民更了解北极地区的情况，因此他们并不满足于仅仅站在一旁，让外部专家来决定一切。

column1: In Canada, where the Inuit people are jealously guarding their hard-won autonomy in the country’s newest territory, Nunavut, they believe their best hope of survival in this changing environment lies in combining their ancestral knowledge with the best of modern science.
column2: 在加拿大，因纽特人悉心守护着他们在该国新设的努纳武特地区争得的自治权。他们相信，要在变化中的环境里生存，最大的希望在于把祖传知识与现代科学的精华结合起来。
column6: newest territory|n. 最新设立的地区
column8: best hope of survival|n. 最大的生存希望
column9: changing environment|n. 变化中的环境

column1: This is a challenge in itself.
column2: 这本身就是一个挑战。

column1: The Canadian Arctic is a vast, treeless polar desert that’s covered with snow for most of the year.
column2: 加拿大北极地区是一片广阔的、无树的极地沙漠，全年大部分时间都覆盖着积雪。

column1: Venture into this terrain and you get some idea of the hardships facing anyone who calls this home.
column2: 如果你深入这片土地，就会了解到那些将这里视为家园的人们所面临的种种困难。

column1: Farming is out of the question and nature offers meagre pickings.
column2: 这里根本无法耕作，大自然所能提供的食物也少得可怜。
column4: out of the question|根本不可能
column7: meagre pickings|n. 少得可怜的收获

column1: Humans first settled in the Arctic a mere 4,500 years ago, surviving by exploiting sea mammals and fish.
column2: 人类直到4500年前才首次在北极定居，靠捕猎海洋哺乳动物和捕鱼为生。
column7: sea mammals|n. 海洋哺乳动物

column1: The environment tested them to the limits: sometimes the colonists were successful, sometimes they failed and vanished.
column2: 环境给了他们最严峻的考验。有些定居者成功立足，有些没能生存下去，最终销声匿迹。
column4: tested them to the limits|使人经受极限考验

column1: But around a thousand years ago, one group emerged that was uniquely well adapted to cope with the Arctic environment.
column2: 但大约一千年前，一个独特地适应北极环境的群体出现了。

column1: These Thule people moved in from Alaska, bringing kayaks, sleds, dogs, pottery and iron tools.
column2: 这些图勒人从阿拉斯加迁来，带来了皮艇、雪橇、狗、陶器和铁制工具。

column1: They are the ancestors of today’s Inuit people.
column2: 他们就是今天因纽特人的祖先。

column1: Life for the descendants of the Thule people is still harsh.
column2: 图勒人的后代至今仍过着艰苦的生活。

column1: Nunavut is 1.9 million square kilometres of rock and ice, and a handful of islands around the North Pole.
column2: 努纳武特有190万平方公里的岩石和冰原，还包括北极点附近的几座岛屿。

column1: It’s currently home to 2,500 people, all but a handful of them indigenous Inuit.
column2: 这里当时住着2500人，除少数人外，都是当地原住的因纽特人。
column3: currently|adv. 在文章所述的当时
column5: all but a handful|除少数人以外全都

column1: Over the past 40 years, most have abandoned their nomadic ways and settled in the territory’s 28 isolated communities, but they still rely heavily on nature to provide food and clothing.
column2: 过去40年间，大多数因纽特人放弃了游居生活，在这块领地上28个偏远的社区定居，但他们所需的食物和衣物仍在很大程度上取自大自然。
column4: nomadic ways|n. 游居的生活方式
column8: rely heavily on|在很大程度上依靠

column1: Provisions available in local shops have to be flown into Nunavut on one of the most costly air networks in the world, or brought by supply ship during the few ice-free weeks of summer.
column2: 当地商店出售的物资需要通过世界上成本最高的航空网络才能运送到努纳武特地区，或者只能在夏季那几个无冰的星期通过补给船进行运输。

column1: It would cost a family around £7,000 a year to replace meat they obtained themselves through hunting with imported meat.
column2: 一家人如果把自家打猎所得的肉换成进口肉，一年大约得花7000英镑。

column1: Economic opportunities are scarce, and for many people state benefits are their only income.
column2: 经济机会十分有限，对许多人来说，政府提供的福利就是他们唯一的收入来源。

column1: While the Inuit may not actually starve if hunting and trapping are curtailed by climate change, there has certainly been an impact on people’s health.
column2: 即使气候变化限制了狩猎和设陷捕猎，因纽特人也未必真会挨饿，但人们的健康确实已经受到了影响。

column1: Obesity, heart disease and diabetes are beginning to appear in a people for whom these have never before been problems.
column2: 肥胖、心脏病和糖尿病正开始出现在因纽特人当中，这些疾病过去从未困扰过这个民族。

column1: There has been a crisis of identity as the traditional skills of hunting, trapping and preparing skins have begun to disappear.
column2: 狩猎、设陷捕猎和处理兽皮的传统技艺开始消失，因纽特人也因此面临身份认同危机。
column3: crisis of identity|n. 身份认同危机

column1: In Nunavut’s ‘igloo and email’ society, where adults who were born in igloos have children who may never have been out on the land, there’s a high incidence of depression.
column2: 在努纳武特这个“冰屋与电子邮件并存”的社会里，有的父母出生在冰屋中，而子女可能从未到过野外。这里的抑郁症发病率很高。

column1: With so much at stake, the Inuit are determined to play a key role in teasing out the mysteries of climate change in the Arctic.
column2: 这件事关系重大。因纽特人决心在解开北极气候变化之谜的过程中发挥关键作用。
column5: play a key role|发挥关键作用

column1: Having survived there for centuries, they believe their wealth of traditional knowledge is vital to the task.
column2: 他们在那里生存了几个世纪，认为自己积累的丰富传统知识对于完成这项任务至关重要。

column1: And Western scientists are starting to draw on this wisdom, increasingly referred to as ‘Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit’, or IQ.
column2: 西方科学家也开始借鉴这种智慧。人们越来越常用因纽特语名称 Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit 来称呼它，简称 IQ。
column7: Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit|n. 因纽特人的传统知识
column8: IQ|abbr. 因纽特传统知识的简称

column1: ‘In the early days scientists ignored us when they came up here to study anything.
column2: “早些年，科学家到这儿来，不管研究什么都不理会我们。

column1: They just figured these people don’t know very much so we won’t ask them,’ says John Amagoalik, an Inuit leader and politician.
column2: 他们就是觉得，‘这些人懂得不多，我们就不问他们了。’”因纽特人领袖、政治家约翰·阿马戈阿利克说。
column4: don’t know very much|懂得不多
column5: won’t ask them|不会去问他们

column1: ‘But in recent years IQ has had much more credibility and weight.’
column2: “不过，近几年，因纽特传统知识的可信度和影响力都提高了许多。”
column4: IQ|abbr. 因纽特传统知识的简称

column1: In fact it is now a requirement for anyone hoping to get permission to do research that they consult the communities, who are helping to set the research agenda to reflect their most important concerns.
column2: 事实上，如今任何人要取得研究许可，都必须先征询当地社区的意见。这些社区正参与制定研究议程，让它体现自己最关心的问题。
column7: set the research agenda|制定研究议程
column9: most important concerns|n. 最关心的问题

column1: They can turn down applications from scientists they believe will work against their interests, or research projects that will impinge too much on their daily lives and traditional activities.
column2: 如果社区认为某位科学家的工作会损害本社区的利益，便可拒绝其申请。对日常生活和传统活动干扰过多的研究项目，社区也可以拒绝。
column5: work against their interests|有损他们的利益
column7: impinge too much on|过度干扰

column1: Some scientists doubt the value of traditional knowledge because the occupation of the Arctic doesn’t go back far enough.
column2: 一些科学家对传统知识的价值持怀疑态度，因为他们认为在北极地区的居住历史并不够悠久，因此这些传统知识缺乏可靠性。

column1: Others, however, point out that the first weather stations in the far north date back just 50 years.
column2: 不过，也有其他人指出，最北端的首批气象站建立至今才刚刚50年而已。

column1: There are still huge gaps in our environmental knowledge, and despite the scientific onslaught, many predictions are no more than best guesses.
column2: 我们对环境的认识还有很大空白。尽管科学研究在大力推进，许多预测也不过是根据现有信息作出的推测。
column4: environmental knowledge|n. 对环境的认识
column6: scientific onslaught|n. 大力推进的科学研究
column9: best guesses|n. 据现有信息所作的推测

column1: IQ could help to bridge the gap and resolve the tremendous uncertainty about how much of what we’re seeing is natural capriciousness and how much is the consequence of human activity.
column2: 因纽特人的传统知识或许能帮助填补这一空白，解开一个至今很难说准的问题：我们所看到的变化，有多少出自自然本身的变幻，又有多少是人类活动造成的？
column3: IQ|abbr. 因纽特传统知识的简称
column7: tremendous uncertainty|n. 极大的不确定性
column8: natural capriciousness|n. 自然界的变幻无常
